scope: Original shared mathematical supplements. Inventory every stated assumption and substantive proof move, identify prerequisites and omissions from natural mathematics before opening any Lean/reconstruction packet. This is not a source fidelity verdict.

units.title: Group weighted fine increments by coarse dyadic cells
units.statement: Fix a positive horizon and nested regular dyadic grids at levels m and n with m≤n. Assign each coarse cell a real weight and each fine cell a real value. The fine sum weighted by the enclosing coarse cell equals the weighted sum of consecutive differences of the fine prefix sums at coarse grid points.
assumptions: The grids are regular dyadic grids of the same positive horizon T. The fine grid refines the coarse grid.
Each wⱼ and zᵢ is an arbitrary real number. The prefix includes the cell ending exactly at its cutoff.

proof.title: Locate the enclosing cell
proof.text: Each fine cell lies inside a unique coarse cell. Its fine right endpoint lies at or before coarse node sₖ exactly when its enclosing coarse cell has index smaller than k.

proof.title: Subtract the two inclusive prefixes
proof.text: The difference selects exactly the fine cells enclosed by the jth coarse cell. Interchanging the finite sums gives the displayed identity.

units.boundary: This identity concerns weights constant within each coarse cell. The continuous-weight approximation is a separate result.

units.title: One almost-everywhere subsequence for countably many limits in measure
units.statement: Suppose a countable family of sequences into a pseudo extended metric space each converges in measure. A single strictly increasing subsequence makes every sequence in the family converge to its stated limit almost everywhere on the same event.
assumptions: The family index type is countable and the sample space carries a measure. The codomain is a pseudo extended metric space.
For each family member, its sequence converges in measure to the specified limit, defined through the measure of each positive extended-distance error event.
units.formula: \exists\,k:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\ \text{strictly increasing},\qquad \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega,\ \forall i,\quad F_{i,k(n)}(\omega)\to G_i(\omega).

proof.title: Choose one index for each tolerance
proof.text: Encode the countable family into natural numbers. For each sequence, the usual geometric error thresholds can be chosen nondecreasing in n. The maximum over codes at most n is then nondecreasing as both the thresholds and the set of codes grow. Adding n makes the selected indices strictly increasing.

proof.title: Intersect the almost-everywhere conclusions
proof.text: For any fixed family member, the error-event measures are summable from the stage at which its code first appears. Borel–Cantelli gives the limit almost everywhere. Intersect over the countable family.

units.boundary: The conclusion is along a single subsequence. Uniform convergence over the family and convergence along the full sequence require separate conditions.

units.title: Stopping at a dyadic grid point selects the increments ending there or earlier
units.statement: Fix a positive time horizon T, a coarse level m and a fine level n at least m. Choose a coarse grid point τ. For any two real paths X and Y on nonnegative time, the fine-grid sum of products of their stopped increments equals the fine-grid prefix sum of their original increment products through τ.
assumptions: The horizon T is positive. Both grids are regular dyadic partitions of [0,T].
The fine level n is at least the coarse level m. The cutoff may be any coarse grid point, including 0 and T.
The two paths are arbitrary real-valued functions of nonnegative time.

proof.title: Find the coarse cell containing each fine cell
proof.text: A fine cell is contained in the coarse cell with index j given by dyadic refinement. If the cutoff is the kth coarse grid point, that cell lies on one side of the cutoff.

proof.title: Evaluate the stopped increment on either side
proof.text: If j is smaller than k, both endpoints keep their original time. Otherwise both endpoints are mapped to τ, and the increment is zero. The inequality on the right endpoint includes a fine cell that ends exactly at τ.

units.boundary: The proof gives a pointwise identity on nested deterministic grids. Convergence of the sum requires a separate probabilistic result.

units.title: Stability of integrated square energy
units.statement: Integrate the squared value of each coordinate over time and add the coordinate energies. The difference between the two random energies is integrable, and its mean absolute value is controlled by the product-space L² norms of the coordinatewise sums and differences.
assumptions: The measure μ is finite, the horizon T is nonnegative, and J is a finite index set.
For every j, both processes are real, progressive for the given filtration, and square integrable on the product of μ and time measure restricted to the deterministic horizon [0,T].

proof.title: Factor the two squares
proof.text: On almost every sample path both squared inputs are integrable in time. Subtract their integrals and factor the difference inside the time integral.

proof.title: Apply Fubini and Cauchy–Schwarz
proof.text: For coordinate j set u=ηⱼ+ξⱼ and v=ηⱼ−ξⱼ. Their product is integrable by Hölder. Move the absolute value inside the time integral, integrate over the product space, and apply Cauchy–Schwarz.

proof.title: Add over coordinates
proof.text: Use the triangle inequality on the finite coordinate sum. The coordinatewise integrability estimates justify exchanging the sum and integral.

units.boundary: The energy is the time integral of the literal process on the stated horizon. The bound uses the L² equivalence classes.

units.title: Quadratic variation of elementary Itô rows
units.statement: At each level of a dyadic grid, take a row of completed Itô integrals of elementary processes on that level's grid. The sum of the squared row increments minus the row's time energy is square integrable at each level and tends to zero in mean absolute value.
assumptions: One Euclidean Brownian motion under the sample measure μ, relative to the given filtration. The coordinates in a finite index set J come from this same motion.
The sample measure is finite. The horizon T is positive and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.

For each level n and coordinate j, the stored dyadic elementary process has level n. Its bounded left-endpoint measurable coefficients have fourth moments bounded by one common real constant C over all n, cells and coordinates.

proof.title: Use the Brownian cell increments
proof.text: The completed scalar integral on a cell equals the stored coefficient times that coordinate's Brownian increment almost surely. Sum this equality over the coordinates.

proof.title: Match the compensator
proof.text: The real energy of each elementary input is exactly the squared coefficient sum weighted by the cell lengths. Thus the actual centered error agrees almost surely with the Brownian grid error.

proof.title: Pass from mean square to mean absolute error
proof.text: The predictable row theorem gives an L² error and convergence of its second moment to zero. The Brownian sample measure is a probability measure, so Cauchy–Schwarz gives the L¹ conclusion.

units.boundary: The elementary input family may change with the level. The fourth moment bound provides uniform control over that family.

units.title: Quadratic variation of a progressive Itô row
units.statement: For one fixed row of progressive square-integrable real inputs, form the sum of their completed coordinate Itô integrals. Its dyadic squared-increment sum converges in L¹ to the total pathwise square energy. The signed error is integrable at every level.
assumptions: One Euclidean Brownian motion under the sample measure μ, relative to the given filtration. The coordinates in a finite index set J come from this same motion.
The sample measure is finite. The horizon T is positive and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
Each coordinate input is real, progressive, and square integrable on the product of μ and time measure restricted to [0,T]. The input row is fixed across levels and can be unbounded.

proof.title: Compare two inputs on the same grid
proof.text: The cell isometry gives square-integrable coordinate increments, so each row increment square is integrable. Fubini gives integrability of the literal path energy. Apply the row increment stability bound and the path energy stability bound to compare two input families on the same grid.

proof.title: Prove the limit at fixed clipping
proof.text: The lagged dyadic approximants have coefficients bounded by M at fixed clipping M. They satisfy the elementary theorem and converge in L² to the clipped integrands. Apply the comparison at each matching level.

proof.title: Remove the clipping
proof.text: Choose M so the comparison error is small uniformly over all levels. Then take the dyadic level large enough for that fixed M.

units.boundary: The conclusion is L¹ convergence along the deterministic dyadic grids over [0,T].

units.title: Sum the Itô energy over a time grid
units.statement: Take a scalar completed Itô integral of a progressive square-integrable integrand. The sum of its squared increments along a finite nondecreasing deterministic grid is integrable. Its expectation is the integrand's squared energy over the half-open span of the grid.
assumptions: On a positive finite time horizon, the given filtration and finite sample measure satisfy the usual conditions used to construct the completed Itô integral.
The integrand is real and progressive with finite product-space squared energy, and the scalar Brownian driver is relative to the given filtration.
The grid satisfies 0 ≤ t₀ ≤ ⋯ ≤ tₙ ≤ T. A grid with no cells and repeated endpoints are allowed.

proof.title: Apply the isometry on each cell
proof.text: The scalar increment is square integrable on each cell. Therefore its square and their finite sum are integrable.

proof.title: Combine the adjacent intervals
proof.text: Exchange the finite sum and integral. The cell intervals are disjoint and concatenate to the grid span. Equal adjacent endpoints contribute an empty interval.

units.boundary: This equality is for the expectation over a fixed deterministic grid. It does not assert a pathwise quadratic-variation identity.

units.title: Square-integrable mixed Brownian increment sums
units.statement: For two distinct coordinates of one Euclidean Brownian motion, the predictably weighted dyadic mixed increment sum is in L² at each level and converges to zero in mean square.
assumptions: One Euclidean Brownian driver and its given filtration.
Distinct coordinates and square-integrable weights measurable at each left endpoint.
One uniform second-moment bound on the weights. T may be zero.
units.formula: C_n=\sum_i w_{n,i}\Delta_i B^j\,\Delta_i B^k,\qquad C_n\in L^2,\qquad \mathbb E[C_n^2]\longrightarrow0.

proof.title: Build a third unit projection
proof.text: Use the normalized sum of the two orthogonal coordinate vectors.

proof.title: Polarize the increments
proof.text: The compensated time terms cancel, leaving the product of the two actual coordinate increments.

proof.title: Transfer the scalar limits
proof.text: The three compensated sums are square integrable. The mixed squared expectation is bounded by a fixed linear combination of their squared expectations.

units.boundary: The actual mixed sum is square integrable on each deterministic grid.

units.title: Isometry on one deterministic Itô cell
units.statement: The increment of the actual completed Itô process between two deterministic times is in L². Its squared expectation equals the probability-time energy of the original integrand on that cell.
assumptions: The progressive real integrand belongs to the probability-time L² domain.
The driver is scalar Brownian relative to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, with finite sample measure and a positive construction horizon T.
The deterministic times satisfy s≤t≤T; the interval may be empty.

proof.title: Use the two terminal representations
proof.text: At each endpoint the actual completed process is the terminal integral of the endpoint-restricted integrand. Linearity puts the increment in L².

proof.title: Identify the restricted process
proof.text: The two restrictions agree before s and after t. Their difference on the intervening cell is the original integrand.

proof.title: Apply the completed isometry
proof.text: The terminal map preserves the L² norm. The square of the indicator-restricted function integrates over the same cell.

units.boundary: The theorem uses deterministic cells and the actual completed scalar Itô process.

units.title: Contract the derivatives with their noise columns
units.statement: For any ambient vector x in d dimensions, the sum of Dσ_j(x)[σ_j(x)] over all coordinates is (2‖x‖²−d−1)x.
assumptions: I is a finite coordinate type with decidable equality. The space is real Euclidean space on I.
Write e_j for the j-th coordinate vector and σ_j(x)=e_j−x_j x.
The vector x is arbitrary and every coordinate column is included.

proof.title: Read the k-th coordinate of one contraction
proof.text: Substitute u=σ_j(x) into the derivative. The j-th component of that direction is 1−x_j².

proof.title: Sum over the coordinate columns
proof.text: The diagonal term contributes x_k once. The last term contributes d copies of x_k, and the squared coordinates sum to ‖x‖².

units.boundary: On the unit sphere the contraction is −(d−1)x. The Stratonovich correction also includes half the squared noise amplitude.

units.title: The projected Hessian trace removes the radial term
units.statement: Let $w$ be a unit vector in a real Euclidean space with finite coordinate set $I$, let $(e_j)_{j\in I}$ be its coordinate basis, and let $f$ be a real ambient test function. Write $p_j=e_j-w_jw$. The trace of the ambient second Fréchet derivative evaluated on the pairs $(p_j,p_j)$ equals the ambient Laplacian minus the radial Hessian entry.
assumptions: The finite coordinate set has decidable equality. The point $w$ has Euclidean norm one.

For an analytic interpretation of the Hessian, take a twice continuously differentiable ambient test near $w$. The Lean equality itself is algebraic in the totalized Fréchet derivatives and has no smoothness premise.

proof.title: Expand the projected arguments
proof.text: Bilinearity gives two mixed radial terms and one term with two radial arguments for each coordinate.
proof.formula: D^2 f[p_j,p_j]=D^2 f[e_j,e_j]-w_jD^2 f[e_j,w]-w_jD^2 f[w,e_j]+w_j^2D^2 f[w,w].

proof.title: Sum the radial contributions
proof.text: The coordinate expansion of $w$ makes each mixed sum equal to the radial Hessian entry. The unit norm makes the squared-coordinate sum one. The remaining diagonal sum is Mathlib's ambient Laplacian.

units.boundary: The equation is pointwise at a unit vector. It concerns the extrinsic trace in ambient coordinates.

units.title: The terminal Itô formula for a unit-sphere diffusion
units.statement: On a positive finite horizon $[0,T]$, form the Euclidean process $X$ from its initial vector, progressive drift integral and completed Brownian coordinate integrals. Assume the process stays on the unit sphere almost surely throughout the horizon. If its drift and noise columns have the spherical coefficients below, then the increment of a twice continuously differentiable ambient test equals the time integral of the sphere generator plus the terminal value of a martingale starting at zero.
assumptions: The coordinate index set is finite with decidable equality. The ambient measure is finite. Brownian motion is standard relative to the filtration, and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.

The initial coordinates are strongly measurable for the time-zero sigma algebra. The drift coordinates are strongly progressive with almost surely integrable time sections. The Brownian integrands are progressive and square-integrable on the horizon.

The process stays on the unit sphere for every time in the horizon on a common full-measure event. A sphere point supplies a measurable fallback for exceptional samples in the compact Itô construction. The test is $C^2$ at each sphere point.

The deterministic temperature is continuous and nonnegative on the horizon. The vector field evaluated along the process has almost surely continuous time paths. Almost surely throughout the horizon the drift is $-u_s-\lambda_s(d-1)X_s$ and the $j$th noise column is $\sqrt{2\lambda_s}(e_j-(X_s)_jX_s)$.

proof.title: Apply the compact Itô formula on the unit sphere
proof.text: The sphere is compact. On the event where all time points are on the sphere, the compact formula uses the original process and yields its two finite-variation integrals and a genuine completed martingale.

proof.title: Identify and combine the integrands
proof.text: On almost every path the drift and Hessian terms are continuous on the compact time interval. Add the two integrals and substitute the pointwise generator identity on the unit states.

units.boundary: The conclusion is a terminal identity for the supplied integrated process on the chosen horizon. Its martingale is existential at this interface. The compact Euclidean formula exposes the actual weighted integrands and their completed-integral representation. Existence of the diffusion and evolution of its marginal laws are separate theorems.

units.title: The quadratic Taylor term converges to the diffusion Hessian contraction
units.statement: Construct a Euclidean process from completed Itô rows. Suppose it stays in compact K almost surely throughout the horizon and the scalar test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at every point of K. The dyadic sum of half the Hessian applied twice to the actual increment converges in measure to the time integral of half the sum of the Hessian on the diffusion columns.
assumptions: The positive horizon is T. The sample measure is finite, the filtration satisfies the usual conditions, and the driving standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The finite coordinate rows have progressive product-square-integrable diffusion coefficients. Their drift evaluations at each fixed time t≤T are almost-everywhere strongly measurable.
Almost every drift path is continuous with bounded variation on [0,T].

The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T]. The test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of K.

notation.text: The process rows use the actual completed integrals. The jth diffusion column has ith coordinate ηᵢⱼ.

proof.title: Use each Hessian entry as a weight
proof.text: The Hessian is continuous on K, so the weight path is continuous on the common event. Compose each measurable slice with the measurable fallback into K, then with the continuous restricted Hessian entry. This representative equals the actual Hessian entry almost everywhere, so the actual weight slice is almost everywhere strongly measurable.

proof.title: Take the coordinate-pair limits
proof.text: Apply continuous-weight covariation to the corresponding completed rows, and sum over the finite set of ordered coordinate pairs.

proof.title: Recover the bilinear evaluations
proof.text: The ordered coordinate expansion recovers the actual quadratic term on each increment and the Hessian on each diffusion column. Product L² gives integrable coefficient products on almost every time section. Continuity bounds the weights on each such sample's compact time interval.

units.boundary: The Hessian-entry bounds use compactness of the time interval along each continuous sample path. The fallback supplies a measurable representative for the fixed-time weights.

units.title: The actual vector Itô Taylor residual vanishes
units.statement: For the completed Euclidean Itô process staying in a compact K throughout the horizon almost surely, and a scalar test twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at every point of K, the sum of second-order Taylor residuals along its dyadic increments converges in measure to zero.
assumptions: The positive horizon is T. The sample measure is finite, the filtration satisfies the usual conditions, and the driving standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The finite coordinate rows have progressive product-square-integrable diffusion coefficients. Their drift evaluations at each fixed time t≤T are almost-everywhere strongly measurable.
The drift paths are almost surely continuous and have bounded variation on [0,T].

The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T]. The test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of that range.

proof.title: Place the paths in the compact range
proof.text: Clip the time at T and apply the Borel fallback outside K. On the event where the original path stays in K, the resulting K-valued path agrees with it at every dyadic grid point.

proof.title: Derive the coordinate square-sum limits
proof.text: At the terminal grid point the inclusive prefix contains all fine cells. The scalar quadratic-variation theorem supplies the limit for each actual coordinate.

proof.title: Apply the Taylor residual estimate
proof.text: Apply the existing Euclidean residual theorem using these coordinate limits. Equality of the clipped and original paths on the grids gives the claimed sum.

units.boundary: The conclusion is convergence in measure on the specified positive horizon. The dyadic residuals are evaluated on the original process.

units.title: The initialized progressive drift has continuous finite-variation paths
units.statement: Let the scalar initial value be strongly measurable at time zero and the scalar drift be strongly progressive. Suppose its time section is integrable on the horizon almost surely. The initial value plus the drift integral is strongly progressive and has almost surely continuous finite-variation paths on the horizon. At every sample and time in the horizon it equals the initialized primitive computed with the fixed horizon measure.
assumptions: T is a nonnegative horizon. The sample space carries a measure and the filtration is indexed by nonnegative time.
The initial value is strongly measurable for the time-zero sigma algebra. The drift is strongly progressive, and almost every drift section is integrable against the horizon time measure.

proof.title: Use one horizon measure for the time primitive
proof.text: On the active time prefix, clipping the drift's time argument at the horizon leaves it unchanged. The two Lean integral expressions agree at every sample. Almost every sample has an integrable time section, where the expressions have their ordinary integrable-path interpretation.

proof.title: Prove the path properties
proof.text: A time-zero measurable initial value gives a constant progressive process. The integral primitive is progressive, continuous along integrable paths and of bounded variation. Adding the initial value leaves each increment unchanged.

units.boundary: The fixed-horizon equality holds at all samples. The continuity and variation conclusions are almost sure.

units.title: Derivative weights of the clipped Euclidean Itô process
units.statement: Take actual completed Euclidean Itô rows with strongly progressive drifts and almost surely continuous drift paths. Evaluate the test derivative on a coordinate basis vector at the time-clipped state, using the fallback when the state is outside K. The weight is strongly progressive, almost surely continuous on the horizon and bounded there by a deterministic constant.
assumptions: The horizon T is positive and the sample measure is finite. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions and the standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The state and Brownian coordinate types are finite with decidable equality. Each diffusion entry is progressive and square-integrable in the product of sample and horizon time measures.
The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T].
The drift coordinates are strongly progressive with almost surely continuous paths on [0,T]. The scalar test is continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of K.

proof.title: Clip time in the progressive domain
proof.text: Clip time at T, keep the state when it belongs to K and use the selected point otherwise. The state replacement is Borel measurable, and agrees with the original state throughout the horizon almost surely.

proof.title: Compose with the derivative entry
proof.text: The derivative entry is continuous on K. Its composition is progressive and almost surely continuous on the horizon. Compactness of K bounds the absolute value uniformly over samples and times.

units.boundary: The drift path condition is almost sure continuity. The deterministic bound applies to the weight evaluated on the state representative.

units.title: The linear Itô term and its completed martingale
units.statement: Take the almost surely compact-range Euclidean process built from initialized drift time primitives and completed stochastic integrals. For a continuously Fréchet differentiable test on that range, the left-endpoint derivative sums converge in measure to the integral of the derivative applied to the drift vector plus the terminal value of a genuine martingale.
assumptions: The horizon T is positive and the sample measure is finite. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions and the standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The state and Brownian coordinate types are finite with decidable equality. Each diffusion entry is progressive and square-integrable in the product of sample and horizon time measures.
The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T].
Each initial coordinate is strongly measurable at time zero. Each drift coordinate is strongly progressive and has almost surely integrable time sections on the horizon.
The scalar test is continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of K.

notation.text: The initial value, moving time primitive and completed Itô integrals define the vector process.
Each gradient entry uses the time-clipped process. The sum of the completed integrals is a martingale starting at zero.

proof.title: Take the drift and noise limits separately
proof.text: For each coordinate use the progressive bounded derivative weight. The actual drift increments are fixed-horizon primitive increments. Apply the weighted time-sum theorem to them and the weighted stochastic-sum theorem to each actual completed integral.
proof.formula: \sum_k W_i(t_k)\Delta A_i\xrightarrow{\mathrm{a.s.}}\int W_i(s)b_i(s)\,ds,\qquad \sum_k W_i(t_k)\Delta I_{ij}\xrightarrow{\mu} I_{\theta_{ij}}(T).

proof.title: Assemble the genuine martingale
proof.text: Each weighted diffusion entry is a progressive L² integrand. Its completed stochastic integral is a martingale. Add them over the finite coordinate pairs. The sum is zero at time zero for every sample.

proof.title: Recover the derivative on the actual vectors
proof.text: The finite limits sum in measure. Expand the derivative on the actual increment in its basis, and move the finite drift sum inside the time integral using bounded weights and integrable drift sections.

units.boundary: This convergence identifies the first-order Taylor term. The quadratic term and the residual enter the full identity separately.

units.title: The weak forward equation from a martingale balance
units.statement: Let P be a probability law on a measurable sample space and E a compact second-countable topological space with its Borel sigma algebra. Let X be a jointly measurable process on nonnegative time with values in E and continuous paths almost surely. Let g be a continuous real test, A a jointly continuous real field on time and state, and M a real martingale for a filtration on nonnegative time under P. Suppose that for each fixed t≥0, the increment g(X_t)−g(X_0) equals the time integral of A(v,X_v) plus M_t−M_0 almost surely. At every s≥0, the expectation of g(X_t) has derivative within the nonnegative half-line equal to the expectation of A(s,X_s).
assumptions: The time parameter is nonnegative and the state space is compact, second-countable and Borel. The process is jointly measurable.
A single almost-sure path continuity statement holds for the whole nonnegative time domain.
The real test g is continuous, and the drift field A is jointly continuous in time and state.
M is a real martingale for the stated filtration and law. For each fixed t, the displayed pathwise increment identity holds almost surely at that t.

proof.title: Center the martingale increment
proof.text: Both martingale values are integrable and have the same expectation. Their difference therefore provides an integrable centered residual in the stated path balance.

proof.title: Apply the centered-balance derivative theorem
proof.text: The centered-balance theorem derives the integral balance by Fubini and differentiates the continuous expected drift. Apply it to the same process, test and drift observable.

units.boundary: At s=0 the derivative is right-sided. The increment identity is supplied at each fixed time. It can come from an Itô formula or another martingale representation.

units.title: When the two Itô generator terms are time integrable
units.statement: Let $v$ be the vector with the given scalar drift rows and $\sigma_j$ the vector with the $j$th given noise column. Both generator terms displayed below are integrable in time for almost every sample.
assumptions: The sample measure $\mu$ is finite. Time is nonnegative and the fixed horizon $T$ may equal zero. The coordinate set $I$ and noise index set $J$ are finite, with decidable equality on $I$. The filtration is indexed by nonnegative real time.

Each drift coordinate has integrable time sections for $\mu$-almost every sample. Each noise entry is a strongly progressive integrand with $L^2(\mu\otimes\ell_T)$ membership, where $\ell_T=\mathrm{Leb}|_{[0,T]}$.
The Euclidean path $X$ is almost surely continuous on $[0,T]$ and almost surely stays in the set $K$ at all horizon times. The ambient test $f$ is $C^2$ at each point of $K$.

proof.title: Control coordinate products
proof.text: Cauchy–Schwarz on the sample-time product gives integrability of each product of two entries in the same noise column. Fubini gives integrability of the time sections.

proof.title: Control the derivative weights
proof.text: Along each selected continuous path, each evaluation of the first or second derivative on basis vectors is continuous and bounded on the compact horizon.
proof.detail: Use the derivative continuity supplied by ContDiffAt and compactness of Icc.

proof.title: Sum over coordinates
proof.text: Expand the linear and bilinear forms in the finite Euclidean basis. Every summand is integrable, and the scalar factor one half preserves integrability.
proof.detail: Use the Euclidean coordinate expansions and integrable_finsetSum.

units.boundary: The result establishes samplewise time integrability on the specified horizon.

units.title: A uniform Taylor residual estimate on a compact set
units.statement: For every ε>0, there is one radius δ>0 that controls the second-order residual for every starting point x in K and every increment with norm less than δ.
assumptions: Let E and F be real normed vector spaces. Derivatives are real Fréchet derivatives; D²f(x) is viewed as a continuous bilinear map.
E is locally compact, K⊆E is compact, and f is C² at every point of K. The set K may be empty.

proof.title: Choose a compact neighborhood inside the smooth locus
proof.text: The C² locus is open. Compactness of K and local compactness of E give a compact closed neighborhood of K contained in that locus.

proof.title: Use uniform continuity of the Hessian
proof.text: The Hessian is continuous on this compact neighborhood, so a single distance threshold bounds its oscillation by ε.

proof.title: Keep every short segment in the neighborhood
proof.text: Take δ=min(ρ,δ₀). Every x+tv with x∈K, ‖v‖<δ and t∈[0,1] remains in the chosen neighborhood and within δ₀ of x. Apply the preceding segment estimate.

units.boundary: The required C² hypothesis is ambient at each point of K, stronger than merely having derivatives relative to K. No global derivative bound is assumed.

units.title: The extrinsic sphere Laplacian expression
units.statement: For a finite coordinate set I, define the following ambient real-valued expression for every f:ℝᴵ→ℝ and w∈ℝᴵ. On the unit sphere and for a C² ambient test this is the usual extrinsic formula for the sphere Laplacian.
assumptions: I is finite with decidable equality, E is Euclidean space ℝᴵ, f:E→ℝ and w∈E. The subtraction |I|−1 is natural-number subtraction before conversion to ℝ.

proof.title: Remove radial second and first derivatives
proof.text: The definition subtracts the radial Hessian and the radial first-derivative correction from the ambient Laplacian.

units.boundary: The definition is total off the sphere and without a smoothness assumption. It is an ambient expression; this declaration does not independently identify an intrinsic Laplace–Beltrami operator.

units.title: The chosen representative agrees on the set
units.statement: If x∈K, forgetting the subtype membership proof in r(x) gives exactly x.
assumptions: E is a type, K⊆E, and k₀ is a specified member of K. The result does not assume compactness.
x is a point of E belonging to K.

proof.title: Select the membership branch
proof.text: The membership hypothesis selects the first branch of the definition, whose underlying value is x.

units.boundary: Agreement is pointwise on K and does not claim agreement outside K.

units.title: Vanishing Taylor residuals on a dyadic time grid
units.statement: For a compact-state process on [0,T], the sums of second-order Taylor residuals over the dyadic grids converge in measure to zero whenever the sums of squared increments converge in measure to a real-valued Q.
assumptions: The sample space Ω carries a finite measure μ. E is a locally compact real normed space with its Borel measurable structure. K⊆E is compact.
f:E→ℝ is C² at every point of K. Each time evaluation of the K-valued process X is measurable. Its paths are continuous on the specified compact time domain for μ-almost every sample.
T>0, X is defined at all nonnegative times and has almost-sure continuous paths on [0,T]. The dyadic sums of squared increments converge in measure to Q:Ω→ℝ.

proof.title: Restrict time to the compact interval
proof.text: Every dyadic time lies in [0,T]. Restrict X to this interval, retaining measurable time slices and almost-sure path continuity.

proof.title: Verify the mesh hypothesis and apply the grid theorem
proof.text: Consecutive grid points are exactly T/2ⁿ apart, so their distances tend to zero. All hypotheses of the arbitrary-grid residual theorem now hold.

units.boundary: This theorem transfers an assumed square-increment limit to a Taylor-residual limit; it does not itself prove quadratic variation for a stochastic integral.
